summary: Day Journal keeps one journal entry per day. The user writes or edits today's entry, browses earlier days newest first, and saves all entries to a Markdown file the user chooses. Entries are stored on the device and restored after restart.
targetUsers: People who keep a daily personal journal
Writers who want a plain Markdown copy of their journal
goals: Keep exactly one journal entry per calendar day
Let the user write or edit today's entry
Let the user browse earlier entries newest first
Save all entries to a Markdown file the user chooses
Keep entries on the device and restore them after restart

features.name: Today's entry editor
features.userOutcome: The user writes or edits the journal entry for today.
features.trigger: The user opens the app or selects today's entry.
features.behavior: The main screen shows today's entry for the current calendar day. If no entry exists for today, the editor starts empty and the first save creates the entry with its date set to today. The editor holds one long-text body. The user types or changes the body and saves; saving updates the stored body for today's date. The entry's date is set by the app to today and is not editable. The body may be empty when saved. The editor shows the date of the entry being edited as a calendar day written YYYY-MM-DD.
features.failureOutcome: If saving today's entry fails, the editor keeps the typed text and shows that the entry was not saved.
acceptanceSignals: Saving today's entry and reading it back from the store returns the same body text and today's date.
Opening the app on a day with no stored entry shows an empty editor, and saving creates exactly one entry for that date.
A failed write leaves the previously stored body unchanged.

features.name: Earlier entries list
features.userOutcome: The user browses earlier journal entries newest first.
features.behavior: Below the editor the app lists all stored entries ordered newest first by entry date. Each row shows the entry date written YYYY-MM-DD and the first 80 characters of the body, with an ellipsis when the body is longer. Selecting a row shows that entry read-only with an Edit button; Edit opens the entry in the editor form. When no entries exist the list shows the text 'No entries yet.' The list loads stored entries when the app starts; if that load fails the list shows one message that entries could not be loaded and shows no rows.
features.failureOutcome: If loading stored entries fails, the list shows that entries could not be loaded and shows no rows.
acceptanceSignals: With entries dated 2024-01-01, 2024-01-03, and 2024-01-02 stored, the list returns them in the order 2024-01-03, 2024-01-02, 2024-01-01.
With no stored entries the list shows 'No entries yet.'
Selecting a row shows the entry read-only, and pressing Edit opens the editor form with that entry's body.

features.name: Export to Markdown
features.userOutcome: The user saves all entries to a Markdown file at a location they choose.
features.trigger: The user presses the Export button.
features.behavior: The user chooses where to save a Markdown file in a Save panel. The file starts with the heading '# Day Journal' followed by a blank line. Each entry follows as a level-two heading '## YYYY-MM-DD' with the entry date written YYYY-MM-DD, then a blank line, then the entry body, then a blank line. Entries are written newest first by entry date. When there are no entries the file contains only the heading '# Day Journal' and a blank line. The file is written whole so a failed write leaves any existing file at that location unchanged.
features.failureOutcome: If writing the chosen file fails, the app shows that the export failed and leaves any existing file at that location unchanged.
acceptanceSignals: Exporting two entries dated 2024-01-02 and 2024-01-01 produces a file beginning '# Day Journal' followed by '## 2024-01-02', its body, then '## 2024-01-01' and its body.
Exporting with no entries produces a file containing only '# Day Journal' and a blank line.
A failed write leaves an existing file at the chosen location with its previous contents.

dataObjects.name: Journal entries
dataObjects.purpose: One journal entry per calendar day, kept on the device.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: Kept on the device until the user removes the app's data.

dataObjects.name: Markdown export file
dataObjects.purpose: A Markdown file the user chooses where to save, containing all journal entries.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: Kept at the location the user chooses until the user removes it.

qualityRequirements: The Markdown export writes each entry date as YYYY-MM-DD and separates entries with a blank line.
productConstraints: Exactly one journal entry exists per calendar day.
Entries are stored on the device and restored after restart.
